long_biography.plain_text:
When Triplex Lloyd mounted a hostile bid for William Cook in the 1990s, Andrew Cook fought it off and led a management buyout backed by Electra Fleming. He later bought out the investor, returning the Sheffield manufacturer to complete family control. The episode capped a transformation begun after he became chairman, when acquisitions turned a modest steel foundry into a broader industrial group.

Cook studied law at University College London, was called to the Bar and completed a technical apprenticeship before joining the business. Beyond industry, he has written company history, fiction and memoir, and led the restoration of a French steam locomotive and vintage carriages. His long commitment to British cast-metals manufacturing was recognised with the CBE and a knighthood.
